The collection covers painting, sculpture, furniture and objets d'art from Antiquity to the 20th century, with icons, medieval and Renaissance sections and works by Rembrandt, Delacroix, Berthe Morisot, Rodin, Cézanne, Mary Cassatt and Monet; it includes 302 Sèvres pieces shown at the 1904 Saint-Louis exhibition and then given by the state to the city (museum website;

Private foundation for modern and contemporary art on a hillside at Saint-Paul-de-Vence near Nice, in buildings by the Catalan architect Josep Lluís Sert with a 2024 underground extension by Silvio d'Ascia (Art Basel, 22 August 2024).

The national opera and ballet company of France, performing in two Paris houses, the Palais Garnier on the Place de l'Opéra and the Opéra Bastille on the Place de la Bastille, and directed by Alexander Neef (Opéra website).

The collection has four parts: the Arts of the Book and Calligraphy, from the fourteenth to the twentieth century, begun with the purchase of a calligraphic panel by Sultan Mahmud II and enlarged in the 1980s by buying private collections; a Painting Collection begun by Sakıp Sabancı in the 1970s, from Ottoman-era to Republican painting;

An archaeological museum of ancient Egypt in downtown Cairo, called the Tahrir museum by AFP, in a building by the French architect Marcel Dourgnon, chosen in an international competition in 1895 (Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities).
Iran's national archaeology museum in Tehran, made up of two museums: the Museum of Ancient Iran and the Museum of Islamic Archaeology and Art of Iran (Blooloop, Museum Influencer List 2020).

The collection held 1,800 works in May 2024, of modern and contemporary Arab art with a stress on forgotten Arab modernists and women artists; nearly 100 works were then out on loan and 122 hung at the Sharjah Art Museum, 68 by women and 54 by men (The Art Newspaper, 14 May 2024).
Bahrain's national museum, on an artificial peninsula facing Muharraq, next to the Bahrain National Theatre (Bahrain Confidential, 14 May 2026).
Russia's state opera and ballet theatre in Moscow, captioned the State Academic Bolshoi Theater by The Moscow Times (2 May 2022).

The collection holds more than 42,000 pieces, of which Kvadrat 500 shows about 1,700 in 28 halls: Christian art from the Bulgarian lands of the 4th to 19th centuries, Bulgarian art of the 19th and 20th centuries, European art of the 15th to 20th centuries, art from Asia, Africa and America, 21st-century art and a graphics collection (gallery website).
A private art museum at 15 Primăverii Boulevard, Bucharest, in a building of 1,200 sqm on five floors (museum website) by the Lebanese architect Youssef Tohme (The Art Newspaper, 22 October 2018).
A theatre, concert hall and museum in one building on Avenida Juárez at Eje Central in the historic centre of Mexico City;

Mexico's national art museum at Tacuba 8 in the historic centre of Mexico City, in the former headquarters of the Secretaría de Comunicaciones y Obras Públicas, built from 1904 to 1911 under the Italian architect Silvio Contri (museum website).
Brazil's national fine arts museum at Avenida Rio Branco 199, Cinelândia, in central Rio de Janeiro, in a building of 20,958 m² (Ibram museum page;

The collection comprises over 33,000 objects from the Middle Ages to the 21st century, with paintings, drawings, prints, sculpture and decorative arts; the gallery names its Impressionist and Post-Impressionist paintings as its main holding, among them Manet's A Bar at the Folies-Bergère (1882) (museum website, collection page).

It has no collection of its own: it shows the national collection of British art from 1500 to the present day and international modern and contemporary art, over 70,000 artworks held by Tate (museum website, collection page).

Tate St Ives is the Tate gallery in Cornwall, in a building by Eldred Evans and David Shalev on the site of a former gasworks overlooking Porthmeor Beach, extended by Jamie Fobert Architects in a project completed in summer 2017 (museum website, history page).
Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum is Glasgow's civic museum on Argyle Street, with 22 galleries covering art, animals, Ancient Egypt, Charles Rennie Mackintosh and more (museum website).
H'ART Museum is an art museum in the former Amstelhof, a 17th-century building on the Amstel in Amsterdam, with an inner garden and a Grand Café (museum website).

Fotografiska is a venue for photography exhibitions in the Royal Customs House (Stora Tullhuset) at Stadsgårdshamnen 22 on the Stockholm waterfront, with a restaurant, bar and shop (museum website; press release on its 15th year).

The collections of paintings and sculptures comprise some 16,000 works from the late Middle Ages to the early 20th century, with an emphasis on Swedish 18th and 19th century painting, Dutch 17th century painting and French 18th century art; artists named include Rembrandt, Rubens, Goya, Renoir, Degas, Gauguin, Carl Larsson and Anders Zorn (museum website, collections page).
The applied arts and design collection has about 30,000 objects from the 14th century to today, a third of them ceramics (museum website, collections page).

The collection includes nearly 30,000 works and is the largest collection of paintings and sculptures in Finland; it runs from 18th century Rococo portraiture to 20th century movements, with more than 650 works of international art (museum website, collection page).

The Acropolis Museum is at 15 Dionysiou Areopagitou in Athens; its exhibition areas run over three levels above an archaeological excavation of an ancient Athenian neighbourhood, visible through glass floors (Greek National Tourism Organisation).

It houses over 45,000 exhibits from the founder's collection and later donors, in six core collections; the Greek section alone has over 33,000 works from antiquity to the Asia Minor Catastrophe of 1922, and the childhood, toys and games collection has 15,000 items (Greek National Tourism Organisation).
Portugal's national museum of art from the Middle Ages to the early nineteenth century, in the Palácio Alvor on Rua das Janelas Verdes, Lisbon (museum website).
A public centre for contemporary culture at Carrer de Montalegre, 5, in the Raval, in the former Casa de Caritat hospice, remodelled from 1991 by Helio Piñón and Albert Viaplana (CCCB website).

The collection has more than 19,000 works: about 15,000 works on paper (drawings, prints, posters and photographs), more than 2,000 paintings, close to 500 sculptures and about 800 decorative arts pieces, among them the Palacio collection of oriental art and Manises ceramics of the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries; it began with deposits from the provincial council, the city, the state and private donors (museum website).

Centro Andaluz de Arte Contemporáneo

A museum of Pablo Picasso's work in the Palacio de Buenavista, a sixteenth-century palace in the old centre of Málaga, extended with new buildings by Richard Gluckman with Cámara Martín Delgado Arquitectos (museum website).
An opera house in the centre of Milan, in the building designed by Giuseppe Piermarini, restored by Mario Botta and Elisabetta Fabbri and reopened on 7 December 2004 (theatre website).
A museum of Egyptian antiquities at Via Accademia delle Scienze 6, Turin, in the Collegio dei Nobili, a building begun in 1679 to a design by Michelangelo Garove (museum website).

The collection: ancient sculptures, bas-reliefs and mosaics, and paintings and sculptures from the fifteenth to the nineteenth century, with paintings by Caravaggio, Raphael, Titian, Correggio, Antonello da Messina and Giovanni Bellini and sculptures by Gian Lorenzo Bernini and Canova; more than 260 paintings are kept in the storerooms (museum website).
An art collection and school on the Benjamin Franklin Parkway in Philadelphia, in a building by Tod Williams Billie Tsien Architects (museum website).
A contemporary art museum in the Allapattah neighbourhood of Miami, in six connected former industrial warehouses converted by Selldorf Architects, with 36 galleries on one level (museum website).

The collection is about 350 works from antiquity to the 20th century: European paintings, Egyptian and classical antiquities, and Asian, Precolumbian and African art; it grew from the Kimbells' 18th and 19th century British pictures and includes Duccio's The Raising of Lazarus, La Tour's The Cheat with the Ace of Clubs and Caravaggio's The Cardsharps, bought in 1987; it does not collect art made after the 1930s or North American art (Google Arts & Culture partner page;

The collection is more than 40,000 works across 5,000 years, in African, American, ancient, Chinese, Japanese, South and Southeast Asian, European, Native American, modern, contemporary, photography and decorative arts departments, plus the Donald J.
An art museum at 4400 Forbes Avenue in Pittsburgh, one of the four Carnegie Museums with the Carnegie Museum of Natural History, the Kamin Science Center and The Andy Warhol Museum (museum website;
A public art museum in Forest Park, St.
The museum describes its collection as tracing art worldwide from antiquity to the present, searchable in an online database; the pages read gave no total (museum website).

The collection is more than 25,000 works: American and European painting, the history of glass, ancient Greek, Roman and Egyptian works, Asian, African and medieval art, sculpture, decorative and graphic arts, and modern and contemporary art (Google Arts & Culture partner page).
The collection is more than 73,000 works covering 6,000 years, searchable online (museum website).

The de Young holds American painting, sculpture and decorative arts from the 1600s to now, art from Africa, Oceania and the Americas, costume and textiles, and modern and contemporary art; the Legion holds European painting, sculpture and decorative arts, ancient Mediterranean art and the largest collection of works on paper in the American West (Google Arts & Culture partner pages).

It holds about 12,000 objects from the combined Pasadena Art Museum and Simon collections and shows about 1,000; holdings include a 1953 bequest of some 500 German Expressionist works from Galka Scheyer and Simon's purchases of Memling, Raphael, Canaletto, Fragonard, Goya, Ingres and Renoir (LAist, 21 December 2025;
A university art museum on Chapel Street in New Haven, housed in three historic buildings designed by four architects, free and open to the public (museum website).

The Fogg holds western paintings, sculpture, decorative arts, photographs, prints and drawings from the Middle Ages to the present; the Busch-Reisinger holds Austrian Secession art, German expressionism, 1920s abstraction and Bauhaus material; the Sackler was built for the collections from Asia, the Middle East and the Mediterranean (museum website).

The collection was assembled from the 1890s with the adviser Bernard Berenson and runs from Italian Renaissance art to textiles, Chinese sculpture, rare books and French paintings of the 1800s (museum website).
A museum of art and culture at 161 Essex Street in Salem, Massachusetts, with a Collection Center in Rowley (museum website).

An art museum in Williamstown, Massachusetts, whose campus includes the Museum Building and the Manton Research Center, joined by a 1973 addition designed by Pietro Belluschi and The Architects Collaborative (iBerkshires, 28 October 2024).

The collection holds more than 50,000 works spanning 6,000 years, with named strengths in Fabergé, Art Nouveau and Art Deco, American art, French Impressionist and Postimpressionist art, British sporting art, English silver, and South Asian, Himalayan and African art (museum website).
Phifer brought about 75 paintings; the holdings are called the People's Collection and span more than 5,000 years (museum website;

A museum of international art and design in Charlotte with two sites: Mint Museum Uptown at the Levine Center for the Arts, 500 South Tryon Street, and Mint Museum Randolph at 2730 Randolph Road (museum website).

The collection holds more than 8,900 works in five departments, European, American, Asian, Contemporary and Photography; the Nortons' gifts form its core, and later purchases include Stuart Davis's New York Mural, acquired in 1964, and a Jackson Pollock acquired in 1971 (museum website).

The collection has grown from about 875 works in 1927 to approximately 55,000 pieces spanning 5,000 years, with holdings in Asian art, American and European painting, works on paper, textiles, and works from Africa, Oceania and the Americas (museum website).

In 2011 The Contemporary Museum, founded by Thurston Twigg-Smith and his family in 1988 in Spalding House, gave its assets and collection to the academy, which took its present name the following year; the director and chief executive is David Odo (museum website).

The collection holds nearly 25,000 works of art and 18,000 films and videos: Ming and Qing dynasty Chinese painting, Mughal Indian miniatures, Baroque painting, old master prints and drawings, early American painting, a core of fifty paintings by Hans Hofmann, works by Rothko, Frankenthaler, Reinhardt, Pollock, David Smith and Clyfford Still, Albert Bierstadt's Yosemite Winter Scene (1872) from Bacon's gift, West Coast avant-garde film, Soviet cinema and what it calls the largest collection of Japanese films outside of Japan (museum website).

The library holds the Ellesmere manuscript of Chaucer's Canterbury Tales (c. 1410), a Gutenberg Bible (c. 1455) and one of two known 1603 editions of Hamlet; the art collection holds eighteenth-century English, American and French paintings, among them Gainsborough's The Blue Boy (c. 1770) (Encyclopedia.com).
A museum of film at 6067 Wilshire Boulevard, Los Angeles, with seven floors, exhibition spaces, a conservation studio and two theatres of 939 and 277 seats (museum website).

A state museum of African American history, art and culture in a 44,000-square-foot building in Exposition Park, a 152-acre tract in south Los Angeles owned by the state, with 15,000 square feet of gallery space (California state budget 2025-26).
The Smithsonian Institution's museum of African American history and culture, at 14th Street and Constitution Avenue NW on the National Mall in Washington (Destination DC).
A concert hall in New York City, on City-owned property, run by the nonprofit Carnegie Hall Corporation (NYC Department of Cultural Affairs;
An opera company performing in the 3,800-seat Metropolitan Opera House at Lincoln Center, New York (ABC7 New York, 21 January 2026).

A nonprofit arts venue in a landmarked armory in New York, built from 1877 to 1881 by the Seventh Regiment of the National Guard, whose main space is the 55,000-square-foot Wade Thompson Drill Hall (Antiques and The Arts Weekly, 10 July 2015;

An independent nonprofit that produces and presents theatre, dance, music, visual art and digital media in a building on West 30th Street between 10th and 11th Avenues, in the Hudson Yards development (BroadwayWorld, 12 January 2023).

A history museum and research library at 170 Central Park West, Manhattan, in a building whose first portion was completed in 1908 and which was expanded on either side in 1938 (The Art Newspaper, 16 June 2026).
A museum of New York City's history at 1220 Fifth Avenue between 103rd and 104th Streets, in a Georgian Colonial-Revival building by Joseph H.

A museum of pre-Hispanic metalwork and archaeology in the historic centre of Bogotá, beside the Parque Santander, in a building opened in 1968 and designed by the Colombian architect Germán Samper Gnecco (My Modern Met).

A municipal art museum on Praça Mauá in the port area of Rio de Janeiro, in two linked buildings: the listed Palacete Dom João VI, which holds the exhibition rooms, and a modernist former bus terminal, which holds the Escola do Olhar.

A natural history and anthropology museum of the Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ), in the Paço de São Cristóvão in the Quinta da Boa Vista, the residence of the imperial family from 1808 to 1889, which it has occupied since 1892 (Agência Gov, 2 April 2025).
What is there: collections of art, archaeology, history and ethnography, from pre-Hispanic artefacts to contemporary art.

Museum of ancient Chinese art in Shanghai with two open sites: the building at 201 Ren Min Da Dao on People's Square and Shanghai Museum East at 1952 Century Avenue in Pudong New Area (museum website).

What is there: 9,078 items in the museum's own collection, 29 of them National Treasures and 207 Important Cultural Properties, plus 6,767 items on long-term loan, 91 of them National Treasures and 620 Important Cultural Properties, as of 31 March 2025; the loans come from temples, shrines and private collectors, and the collection galleries cover ceramics, archaeological relics, paintings, calligraphy, decorative and applied arts and sculpture (National Institutes for Cultural Heritage outline 2025).

What is there: over 6,000 works centred on the Matsukata Collection, from the Middle Ages to the mid twentieth century, with Degas, Van Gogh and Rodin named (National Museum of Art website); the museum's own collection page gives about 5,500 works as of 2015 and says it has bought works every year since it opened.

State museum of the arts, design, science and technology in Sydney, which calls itself the largest museum group in Australia; its sites are Powerhouse Parramatta at 34 Phillip St, Powerhouse Ultimo, the Powerhouse Castle Hill store and Sydney Observatory (museum website).
Museum of natural science and culture at 1 William Street, Sydney, on the corner of William and College Streets opposite Hyde Park (museum website).

Museum and war memorial in Auckland, in a heritage building it has occupied since 1929, with a Grand Foyer, the Te Marae Ātea Māori Court, Pacific galleries and a volcano gallery (RNZ, 11 February 2026 and 16 October 2025).
National museum of Indian art and archaeology on Janpath, New Delhi, under the Ministry of Culture; it opened in 1949 and moved to its current site in 1955 (The Art Newspaper, 6 February 2025).

What is there: over 48,000 art objects dating from the 2nd century BCE to the 20th century, collected by the Salar Jung family and 'majorly collected by Nawab Mir Yousuf Ali Khan popularly known as Salar Jung III' (museum website).
Exhibition building in Dubai whose circular form carries the sayings of Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum in the calligraphy of Mattar bin Lahej on its facade (museum website).
Palace museum on the headland of Istanbul's historic peninsula, at Cankurtaran Mah.

Holocaust remembrance, documentation, research and education centre on 45 acres of the Mount of Remembrance in Jerusalem, with the Holocaust History Museum, the Museum of Holocaust Art, the Hall of Remembrance, the Children's Memorial, the Valley of the Communities and a synagogue (Yad Vashem website).

Archaeological museum in Beirut, 3km south of the port, in a three-storey building constructed between 1930 and 1937; the Nuhad Es-Said Pavilion for Culture, designed by Raed Abillama, stands off its south-western side (The Art Newspaper, 3 August 2021;

What is there: European painting from the 14th to the 18th century, with well over 700 paintings on show in 19 halls and 47 cabinets; named works include Dürer's 'Selbstbildnis im Pelzrock' (1500), Altdorfer's 'Alexanderschlacht' (1529), Leonardo's 'Madonna mit der Nelke' (about 1475), Raphael's 'Heilige Familie aus dem Hause Canigiani', Rubens's 'Das Große Jüngste Gericht' and 'Höllensturz der Verdammten', Rembrandt's 'Jugendliches Selbstbildnis' (1629) and Boucher's 'Madame de Pompadour' (1756) (muenchen.de; museum website).

Museum Brandhorst is a museum of contemporary art in the Kunstareal in Munich, in a building by the Berlin architects Sauerbruch Hutton whose facade is made of 36,000 ceramic rods in 23 colours (museum website).

What is there: painting, sculpture and graphic art covering over 700 years from the Middle Ages to the present, with a focus on classical modernism and works by Picasso, Kandinsky, Beckmann, Schlemmer and Matisse (Stuttgart tourist office).

What is there: about 130,000 objects from antiquity to the present, of which about 800 are shown on over 5,000 square metres: painting to 1900, a graphic collection, sculpture and applied art, 20th and 21st century art, photography, time-based media, and a glass collection of about 13,000 objects; the holdings go back to the graphic collection and parts of the painting gallery of Elector Jan Wellem founded in 1709, and the collection of the Kunstakademie has been in the Ehrenhof since 1932 (museum website).

The Kunst- und Ausstellungshalle der Bundesrepublik Deutschland, short Bundeskunsthalle, is an exhibition house on Bonn's Museumsmeile for art of all periods, cultural history, archaeology and science, with its own programme of theatre, performance, dance and music (museum website).

What is there: departments for the Middle Ages, the Baroque, the 19th century and a graphic collection; the Fondation Corboud, over 170 paintings mainly of Impressionism and Neo-Impressionism, given in March 2001 as a 'perpetual loan' into the care of the City of Cologne by Gérard J.

The history page names the collector Josef Haubrich and the Ludwig collection, added in 1968, as sources of its modern art; the Museum Ludwig was then founded for 20th century art and shared a new building with the Wallraf from 1986 (museum website).
The Sprengel Museum Hannover is a museum of international art of the 20th and 21st centuries with 8,000 square metres of exhibition space (museum website).

The Galerie Neue Meister was founded in 1959 out of the modern department of the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister and has been in the Albertinum since 1965; the Dresden collections have been financed and run by the state since a museum reform in 1831 (museum website).

What is there: over 4,600 paintings, 1,800 sculptures, medals and plaques, over 5,000 photographs and over 70,000 works on paper, from Old Masters such as Frans Hals and Lucas Cranach the Younger to Caspar David Friedrich, Max Beckmann and Max Klinger, with Leipzig art and art of the GDR as a focus; nearly 400 paintings are Dutch 17th century works (museum website).

What is there: European painting from the 13th to the 18th century, about 1,200 works on show in 72 halls and cabinets along a route of nearly two kilometres; strengths in German and Italian painting of the 13th to 16th centuries and Netherlandish painting of the 15th to 17th centuries; 20 works by Rembrandt; named works include Caravaggio's 'Amor als Sieger' (1602), Cranach's 'Der Jungbrunnen' (1546), Giotto's 'Die Grablegung Mariae', Titian's 'Venus mit dem Orgelspieler' and Vermeer's 'Junge Dame mit Perlenhalsband' (museum website).
The Neues Museum is one of the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin on Museum Island, entered through the James-Simon-Galerie on Bodestraße (museum website).

What is there: the Hasso Plattner collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist painting, 115 works by 23 artists, with 40 paintings by Claude Monet, and works by Renoir, Morisot, Sisley, Pissarro, Caillebotte and Signac; named works are Caillebotte's 'Brücke von Argenteuil' (1883), Monet's 'Getreideschober' (1891) and 'Seerosen' (1914 to 1917) and Signac's 'Hafen bei Sonnenuntergang' (1892);

What is there: more than 8,000 antiquities, 3,000 decorative art objects, 50,000 coins and medals, 3,000 paintings, 15,000 works on paper and 1,000 sculptures, from pharaonic Egypt to the 20th century, with works by Veronese, Rubens, Rembrandt, Poussin, Renoir, Monet, Gauguin, Matisse and Picasso.
Museum of natural sciences, human sciences and science and technology at the southern tip of the Lyon peninsula, in a building by the Austrian agency Coop Himmelb(l)au (museum website).

What is there: more than 1,300 paintings, among them Goya's Les Jeunes and Les Vieilles, bought in 1873, with works by David, Delacroix, Courbet, Monet and Rodin; a graphic arts cabinet built on Jean-Baptiste Wicar's bequest of nearly 1,300 drawings, including Raphael's study for the Alba Madonna; antiquities, medieval and Renaissance works; and relief maps of fortified towns of northern Europe at 1:600 (14 by Le Quotidien de l'Art's count, sixteen by the museum's history page), shown under the atrium since 1997 and restored between April 2018 and March 2019 (museum website; scientific and cultural project;

What is there: Flemish and Dutch painting from Fabre's gifts and the bequest of the stockbroker Antoine Valedau (1777-1836); 19th century French painting given mostly by Alfred Bruyas (1821-1877), including Courbet's La Rencontre and Les Baigneuses; works by the Montpellier painters Alexandre Cabanel and Frédéric Bazille; a group of works by Pierre Soulages; and 18th century Montpellier silver (museum website).

Contemporary art museum in two 18th century mansions by Jean-Baptiste Franque in the centre of Avignon, the Hôtel de Caumont and the Hôtel de Montfaucon, made available by the City of Avignon and refitted by Rudy Ricciotti and by Cyrille and Laurent Berger (museum website).

What is there: exhibitions of historical and contemporary photography, the Prix Découverte Fondation Louis Roederer, the Arles Books fair, photography workshops and a portfolio review, and education programmes; the festival also lists a collection on its site (festival website).

Annual theatre and performing arts festival held each July in Avignon and the region, in nearly 40 places including the Cour d'honneur of the Palais des papes; its offices are in the Cloître Saint-Louis and it has its own rehearsal and residency building, La FabricA (festival website; festival document 2026-2030).

National museum of Asian arts on the Chaillot hill in Paris, in the building Émile Guimet had built at place d'Iéna, renovated by Henri and Bruno Gaudin and reopened in 2001; it also runs the Hôtel d'Heidelbach (attached in 1991) and the Musée d'Ennery (attached in 1908), the latter closed for renovation until 2028 (museum website).

What is there: Monet's Nymphéas cycle, and the Jean Walter and Paul Guillaume collection of 148 works from the 1860s to the 1930s: 25 Renoir, 15 Cézanne, 12 Picasso, 10 Matisse, 5 Modigliani, 9 Douanier Rousseau, 30 Derain, 22 Soutine, 10 Utrillo, 6 Marie Laurencin.

What is there: a visit route of about 6,000 objects on seven floors covering eight centuries, from medieval altarpieces to contemporary design, with fashion, jewellery, wallpaper, drawings and a large photographic fonds; the collection grew by 1,273 works in 2023, about 10,000 large works were moved to new stores at Le Bourget, and 5,381 works were on deposit at 112 sites at the end of 2023 (museum website; activity report 2023).

Concert and music complex in the Parc de la Villette, 19th arrondissement of Paris, on two buildings: the Philharmonie, with a 2,500-seat hall (the Grande salle Pierre Boulez), and the Cité de la musique (museum website;

National theatre whose historic stage since the Revolution is the Salle Richelieu at the Palais-Royal, Paris; it also plays at the Théâtre du Vieux-Colombier (since 1993) and the Studio-Théâtre in the Carrousel du Louvre (since 1996) (theatre website).
Foundation for contemporary creation at 9 rue du Plâtre in the Marais, Paris, in a building designed by Rem Koolhaas whose mobile floors change the space (foundation website).
Departmental museum of contemporary art on place de la Libération in Vitry-sur-Seine, south-east of Paris (Centre Pompidou partner page;

What is there: a collection of Spanish contemporary art of more than 1,600 works by Spanish artists, shown in slow rotation at the Museo de Arte Abstracto Español in Cuenca, founded by Fernando Zóbel and now owned by the foundation, and at the Museu Fundación Juan March in Palma, created in 1994; the Madrid building shows temporary exhibitions, held there since 1973, and gives about 150 concerts a season (foundation website).

What is there: three seasons a year of paired exhibitions of painting and photography, on international art from the mid 19th to the mid 20th century and on photographers of the 20th century and the present; the 2025 exhibitions in Madrid had 319,559 visitors (annual accounts 2025).

The Colección Telefónica brings together works of art, technological objects, photographs, documents and audiovisual archives; its art collection, begun in the 1980s with works by Picasso, Juan Gris, Tàpies and Chillida, holds more than 1,100 pieces, with Cubism as its core (María Blanchard, Jean Metzinger), Surrealist holdings (Magritte, Matta) and contemporary photography (foundation collections page).
An opera house on La Rambla in Barcelona, run by the Fundació del Gran Teatre del Liceu on behalf of a consortium of four public administrations (Liceu website; consortium audit 2024/25).
The national archaeology museum of Spain, at Calle Serrano 13 in Madrid, a state museum of the Ministry of Culture (museum website).

The contract brings six semi-permanent exhibitions of 20th and 21st century art from the Centre Pompidou's collection over the decade, two temporary exhibitions a year, a jointly curated show within the Hors Pistes festival and a yearly workshop exhibition for young visitors (Málaga City Council, 11 July 2024).
A concert hall on Avenida da Boavista in Porto, described by the house as the first building in Portugal built only for music, managed by the Fundação Casa da Música (house website).

What is there: more than 18,000 pieces, including about 2,500 paintings from the 16th to the 20th century (Silva Porto, Marques de Oliveira, Henrique Pousão, Aurélia de Souza, António Carneiro), sculpture centred on Soares dos Reis and his 'O Desterrado' (Rome, 1872), northern Portuguese faience, glass, jewellery, textiles and furniture; ten pieces are classed as National Treasures.

The canal house at Prinsengracht 263 to 267 in Amsterdam with the Secret Annex where Anne Frank and seven others hid, entered at Westermarkt 20; an organisation of about 250 employees runs the museum, manages the collection, makes educational material and researches Anne Frank's history (House website).

The Netherlands' national museum for film, in a white building on the north bank of the IJ opposite Amsterdam Central Station, with four cinemas, an exhibition space, an education floor and a bar-restaurant; it has 185 employees (Eye website).

What is there: the National Collection for Dutch Architecture and Urban Planning, about 700 archives of Dutch designers from 1850 onward, with drawings, sketches, working drawings, correspondence, photographs, models, posters and born-digital material; named archives include those of Theo van Doesburg, H.P.
A privately run museum for modern and contemporary art at Buurtweg 90 in Wassenaar, on the Voorlinden estate of woods, dunes and gardens, which visitors can walk (museum website).

The fine arts museum of Flanders, in a building of 1890 by Frans van Dijk and Jean Jacques Winders on the Leopold de Waelplaats in Antwerp, into whose former patios KAAN Architecten fitted a new white museum for art after 1880 (VRT, 15 September 2022).

A museum of modern and contemporary art, architecture and landscape architecture in the former Citroën garage by the canal in Brussels, an Art Deco building of the mid 1930s with 40,000 square metres, which the Brussels-Capital Region bought in October 2015 (Kanal website;
The city museum of Leuven for old and contemporary art, at Leopold Vanderkelenstraat 28 (museum website).
A state museum in Venice, in the complex of the church of Santa Maria della Carità, its monastery and the Scuola Grande of the same name, at Campo della Carità in Dorsoduro (museum website).

The palace of the Doge and the magistracies of the Venetian Republic on the Piazzetta San Marco, Venice, a Gothic building in three blocks with a wing toward the lagoon rebuilt from 1340 and a wing toward the Piazzetta begun in 1424 (museum website).

An opera house at Campo San Fantin in Venice, run by the Fondazione Teatro La Fenice, a non-profit foundation under Legislative Decree 367 of 29 June 1996 whose president is the mayor of Venice (theatre website).

A civic museum of 20th and 21st century Italian art in the Palazzo dell'Arengario on Piazza del Duomo, Milan, a building designed by Griffini, Magistretti, Muzio and Portaluppi and converted by Gruppo Rota (museum website).
The Museo delle Culture of Milan, at Via Tortona 56 in the former Ansaldo factory, a building of 8,000 square metres on three floors designed by David Chipperfield (Arte.it, 8 September 2021;

A centre for contemporary culture and for technology business in the former Officine Grandi Riparazioni, a railway repair works at Corso Castelfidardo 22, Turin, an H-shaped building of about 20,000 square metres and 16 metres high (OGR website).

The Museo di arte moderna e contemporanea di Trento e Rovereto, with its main building at Corso Bettini 43 in Rovereto, designed by Mario Botta with the engineer Giulio Andreolli; it also runs the Casa d'Arte Futurista Depero in Rovereto and the Galleria Civica in Trento (museum website).
A state museum in the royal palace of Capodimonte in Naples, with the Real Bosco, a park of 134 hectares with more than 400 plant species (museum website).

The archaeological site of the Roman city of Pompeii, with the sites of Oplontis at Torre Annunziata, Stabiae at Castellammare di Stabia, the Antiquarium and Villa Regina at Boscoreale, Longola, the Castle of Lettere, the Reggia di Quisisana and the former Royal Bourbon Powder Factory at Scafati (park website).

The archaeological park of central Rome: the Colosseum, the Roman Forum, the Palatine and the Domus Aurea, with the Meta Sudans, the Arch of Constantine, Hadrian's Auditoria and Trajan's Column (added by ministerial decree 380 of 22 October 2021), the Circus Maximus and the Imperial Fora; its boundaries were reset by decree 171 of 17 April 2026 (park website).

The opera foundation of Verona, which stages the Arena di Verona Opera Festival each summer in the Roman amphitheatre on Piazza Bra, with about 30,000 seats by the foundation's count, and a year-round season at the Teatro Filarmonico (foundation website).
ARKEN Museum of Contemporary Art

What is there: Thorvaldsen's own sculptures, models and drawings, his collections of other artists' paintings and sculptures, art, coins and crafts from antiquity, and medals, books and personal items, all from the gift he made to Copenhagen in 1838 (museum website;

Denmark's national stage for ballet, opera, drama and orchestral music, a state enterprise under the Ministry of Culture with three houses in Copenhagen: the Old Stage on Kongens Nytorv, the Opera House on Holmen and the Playhouse on Kvæsthusbroen (annual report 2025; theatre website).

The China collection has about 4,000 objects from the Neolithic to the early 20th century, 2,250 of them given by Johan Wilhelm Normann Munthe, who sent crates from 1907 until his death in 1935 (museum website).

Norway's largest music and performing arts institution, in the opera house at Kirsten Flagstads plass 1 in Bjørvika, Oslo, designed by Snøhetta and opened on 12 April 2008, with a roof the public can walk on (company website;

What is there: the museum's page gives the collection as 3,500 artworks in its introduction and 'over 2,600 works' in its history section; it holds Norway's largest collection of Lars Hertervig, a growing group of paintings by Kitty Kielland, works by Frida Hansen, the Jan Groth collection begun in 1998 with gifts from the artist and added to by Steingrim Laursen's bequest in 2007, and 67 contemporary works given by Trond Mohn in autumn 2012 (museum website).

What is there: Western art from the 15th century to today with the weight on Nordic art, called the third largest art museum collection in Sweden by number of works; the Fürstenberg gallery of Nordic art from the 1880s and 1890s, the Gothenburg Colourists, works by Zorn, Hanna Pauli, Munch, Monet, Gauguin, van Gogh, Chagall, Picasso, Rubens and Rembrandt's 'Riddaren med falken', and about 2,000 children's book illustrations given by the friends' association Barnboksbildens Vänner (museum website).

What is there: more than 40,000 works, mainly from the 15th century to today, of art, craft and design, with works by Alexander Roslin, Carl Fredrik Hill, Anders Zorn, Ester Almqvist, Sigrid Hjertén and Lena Cronqvist, the Russian works from the Baltic Exhibition in Malmö in 1914, international names such as Cindy Sherman, Barbara Kruger, Joseph Beuys and Mike Kelley, and a collection of Nordic contemporary art; only about 2% can be shown in the present rooms (City of Malmö website).
A municipal art hall at Djurgårdsvägen 60 on Djurgården in Stockholm, in a building by the architect Carl Bergsten, with the extension Liljevalchs+ behind it on Falkenbergsgatan 3 (art hall website).

Sweden's national stage for theatre, in the theatre house on Nybroplan in Stockholm (Thaliahuset, with the adjoining Hansahuset), with the stages Stora scenen, which seats 770, Lilla scenen, Målarsalen, Lejonkulan and Tornrummet (theatre website; annual report 2025).

Sweden's national stage for opera and ballet, in the opera house on Gustav Adolfs torg in Stockholm, inaugurated in 1898, which the National Property Board (Statens fastighetsverk) is to renovate (company website; government press release, October 2025).

What is there: more than 10,000 works belonging to the residents of Helsinki, mostly Finnish art of the 20th and 21st centuries with some older Finnish works and international art, made up of several donated collections and the city's own purchases; the Leonard and Katarina Bäcksbacka Collection, donated in 1976, has its own halls, with Tove Jansson's frescos also on view; the collection includes the city's public art in streets, squares, parks and public buildings (museum website).
Finland's national opera and ballet company, in the Opera House at Helsinginkatu 58 by Töölönlahti bay in Helsinki, its home since 1993 (company website).

What is there: about 16,000 works, of which more than 10,000 are works on paper, the oldest from the 16th century and most from the 19th and 20th centuries (working group report, April 2024); the gallery's own page says approximately 15,000 works, with Icelandic artists such as Jóhannes Kjarval and Louisa Matthíasdóttir and works by Picasso, Munch, Ólafur Elíasson, Karin Sander and Roni Horn (museum website).
A concert hall and conference centre at Austurbakka 2 by the old harbour in central Reykjavík, with a glass facade by Ólafur Elíasson and the main concert hall Eldborg (company website).

What is there: no art museum collection in the usual sense, the members run the programme in six sections (visual arts, architecture, music, literature, performing arts, film and media art); the house at Hanseatenweg was given by the German-American Henry H.

Berliner Festspiele organises festivals, exhibitions, concerts, dance and theatre through the year, in the Haus der Berliner Festspiele at Schaperstraße 24 and the Gropius Bau at Niederkirchnerstraße 7 (Berliner Festspiele website).
The Maxim Gorki Theater is a spoken theatre at Am Festungsgraben 2 in Berlin Mitte (theatre imprint).

The Staatsoper Unter den Linden is an opera house at Unter den Linden 7 in Berlin Mitte, one of the houses of the Stiftung Oper in Berlin with the Deutsche Oper, the Komische Oper, the Staatsballett and the Bühnenservice (Staatsoper website).
The Bayerische Staatsoper is the state opera of Bavaria, playing in the Nationaltheater at Max-Joseph-Platz 2 in Munich (German Music Information Centre, miz.org).
The Münchner Kammerspiele is the spoken theatre of the City of Munich, with its box office at Maximilianstraße 26-28; it calls itself a 'Theater der Stadt' (Kammerspiele website).

The Burgtheater is a spoken theatre at Universitätsring 2 in Vienna, opposite the city hall, which its site calls the largest German-language spoken theatre; it is one of the houses of the Austrian federal theatres group (Burgtheater website;
The Wiener Staatsoper is an opera and ballet house at Opernring 2 in Vienna, run as Wiener Staatsoper GmbH;
The Salzburger Festspiele is a summer festival of opera, drama and concerts in Salzburg, run by the Salzburger Festspielfonds at Hofstallgasse 1 (festival website).
The Heidi Horten Collection is a private museum at Hanuschgasse 3 in Vienna, in a house with a neoclassical facade and a small sculpture garden in the Hanuschhof (museum website).
The Museum der Moderne Salzburg is a museum of modern and contemporary art at two sites, Mönchsberg 32 and the Rupertinum at Wiener-Philharmoniker-Gasse 9 (museum website).

The Zentrum Paul Klee is a museum and research centre for the life and work of Paul Klee at Monument im Fruchtland 3 in Bern, in a building by Renzo Piano on a site of 90,000 square metres (Zentrum Paul Klee website).
MAMCO is Geneva's museum of modern and contemporary art, placed under a public foundation created by law L 9418 of the Grand Conseil of Geneva of 18 December 2004 (MAMCO website).

What is there: 5,637 objects from the fifteenth to the nineteenth centuries, shown in twenty-seven rooms and galleries: 777 pictures, 317 miniatures, 525 pieces of furniture, 481 sculptures, 1,342 pieces of European arms and armour, 1,057 of Oriental arms and armour, 287 pieces of porcelain, 89 gold boxes and more, with French eighteenth-century art, princely arms and armour and Old Master paintings as the main holdings; named works include Fragonard's The Swing (1767) and Frans Hals's Laughing Cavalier (1624) (annual report 2024-25;

The London branch and headquarters of Imperial War Museums, on Lambeth Road in south London; the group has five sites: IWM London, IWM North, IWM Duxford, Churchill War Rooms and HMS Belfast (annual report 2025-26).
A museum and public gardens in Forest Hill, south London, with an aquarium and butterfly house; the museum and gardens are free, the aquarium and butterfly house are ticketed (museum website).
The University of Oxford's museum of art and archaeology, on Beaumont Street, Oxford, with free entry (museum website).
The University of Cambridge's principal museum of art and antiquities, on Trumpington Street, Cambridge, with free entry to collections and displays (museum website).
The University of Oxford's museum of anthropology and world archaeology, reached through the Oxford University Museum of Natural History on Parks Road, with free entry (museum website).

What is there: more than 25,000 works of fine and decorative art and a collection of over 46,000 objects spanning six centuries, with Pre-Raphaelite paintings, early twentieth-century British art including Lowry, and about 50 couture pieces;

What is there: Renaissance paintings, Tudor portraits, sculpture, Victorian and Pre-Raphaelite art, Victorian decorative arts and contemporary works; the Renaissance Rediscovered galleries opened in 2023 as part of a long-term refurbishment (Art Fund;

What is there: art from the Renaissance, the Dutch Golden Age, the Pre-Raphaelites and the modern period; history, science and industry; natural history; ethnography from Africa, Asia and the Americas; archaeology including ancient Egypt and Rome; and the Staffordshire Hoard of over 3,500 pieces of 7th-century Anglo-Saxon gold and silver, found in 2009.

What is there: The art collection spans about five hundred years of paintings, drawings, sculpture, silver and ceramics and includes what the museum calls 'one of Europe's best collections of Impressionist art'; the Evolution of Wales and Natural History galleries hold the science collections.

What is there: about 9,000 objects: Chinese art, described as one of the most significant holdings in the UK; medieval stained glass, arms and armour; more than 200 tapestries and about 150 carpets, including the Wagner garden carpet; and late 19th-century French paintings with more than 20 works by Degas, Manet's Roses in a Champagne Glass (1882) and Cézanne's The Chateau of Medan (1879 to 1880) (museum website;

Scotland's design museum, at 1 Riverside Esplanade on Dundee's waterfront, with free admission; the 8,000 square metre building, with 1,650 square metres of gallery space, was designed by Kengo Kuma & Associates, chosen by international competition, and cost £80.11m to design, build and fit out (museum website).

Under legal deposit the library receives a copy of everything published in the UK and Ireland, and the UK Web Archive holds more than 1.5 petabytes; in June 2025 it acquired five medieval manuscripts from Longleat House with a grant from the National Heritage Memorial Fund (library website; annual report 2025-26).

Queensland's state opera company, founded in 1981 as the Lyric Opera of Queensland with Queensland Government funding, after the Queensland Opera Company closed in December 1980; it was renamed Opera Queensland in 1996 (Wikipedia).

Founded on 20 January 1862 by the Queensland Philosophical Society; it opened at its current site in the Queensland Cultural Centre, South Bank, in 1986, and "Kurilpa" was added to its name in 2023 (Wikipedia).

John Christie and his wife, the soprano Audrey Mildmay, opened an opera theatre at Glyndebourne, a country house near Lewes, and the first season began on 28 May 1934 with Le nozze di Figaro (Wikipedia).

The library began in 1896 as the Brisbane Public Library, was renamed the Public Library of Queensland in 1898 and moved to its South Bank site in 1988; the John Oxley Library, a research centre for Queensland material, opened in 1934 (Wikipedia).
Built as a Church of Christ, Scientist, completed in 1907 to designs by Robert Fellowes Chisholm; the building was Grade II listed in April 1969 (Wikipedia).

The Altes Museum is a museum of classical antiquity in Berlin, housed in a building by Karl Friedrich Schinkel built from 1823 to 1830, with 18 Ionic columns and a rotunda that refers to the Pantheon (museum website).
Bauhaus-Archiv / Museum für Gestaltung
The Deutsches Theater is a repertory theatre at Schumannstraße in Berlin with three stages: the large stage of about 650 seats, the Kammer of about 230 and the Box of up to 80 (theatre website).

The Komische Oper Berlin is an opera house whose main building is on Behrenstraße in Mitte; since 2023 it has performed at the Schillertheater, Bismarckstraße 110 in Charlottenburg, with about 20% fewer seats (opera website;
The Deutsche Oper Berlin is an opera house in Charlottenburg, Berlin; its site names Aviel Cahn as Intendant (opera website).

The Thalia Theater is one of Hamburg's four Staatstheater, at Alstertor in the city centre, with a main house of about 1,000 seats and a studio in the Gaußstraße in Altona with 200 (theatre website; hamburg.de).

The Schauspielhaus Zürich is a theatre company with two main venues, the Pfauen and the Schiffbau (with the Halle and the Matchbox), run by Schauspielhaus Zürich AG; the site marks 100 years of the Pfauenbühne (theatre website).

The Bregenzer Festspiele stage opera on the Lake Stage (Seebühne) and productions in the Festspielhaus on Lake Constance in Bregenz; total capacity across venues is 11,497 seats (festival facts and figures).
The Kunstforum Wien is an exhibition house at Freyung 8 in Vienna's first district, operated by UniCredit Bank Austria (LEADERSnet, 2 February 2025;
TBA21 (Thyssen-Bornemisza Art Contemporary)
The Museum Rietberg is a museum of non-European art at Gablerstrasse 15 in Zurich; its tagline is 'World Art in Zurich' (museum website).
The Fondation Pierre Gianadda is a museum and cultural centre at Rue du Forum 59 in Martigny, Valais, with a Gallo-Roman museum, an automobile museum and a sculpture park (foundation website).
What is there: the MCBA's permanent display includes some three hundred works from the eighteenth century to the present; the pages read gave no collection figures for mudac or Photo Elysée.
What is there: two or three major exhibitions a year, often Impressionists and others such as Degas and Gauguin, and a permanent collection of Chinese porcelain in the basement (Lausanne Tourisme).
A museum on Nishi-shinjuku, Tokyo; since July 2020 it has been in a six-story building on neighbouring land (museum website).

What is there: modern Japanese paintings with Yokoyama Taikan first among the artists, contemporary Japanese paintings, ceramics by Kitaoji Rosanjin, children's picture books and wood carvings (museum website).
Japan's national theatre for the contemporary performing arts, in Tokyo (theatre website).
The war museum run by the Korea War Memorial Organization in Seoul (Korea Times, 9 June 2026).
A public art museum in Ueno Park, Tokyo (museum website).
The provincial museum of Guangdong in the Cultural and Art Square, Zhujiang New Town, Tianhe District (China Daily).
A performing arts centre in central Seoul with six resident arts groups (Asia Economy, 20 October 2022).
A theatre complex of 21.75 hectares beside a lake at 2 West Chang'an Avenue, Beijing (China Daily).
The Musée Carnavalet - Histoire de Paris is the City of Paris history museum at 23 rue Madame de Sévigné, in two mansions of the Marais (museum website; press kit).
The Musée de l'Homme is an anthropology museum at 17 place du Trocadéro, Paris (museum website).
What is there: the Cast Gallery of the Musée des Monuments français, a Modern and Contemporary Architecture Gallery and a Murals and Stained Glass Gallery (institution's website).

The Théâtre de la Ville is a Paris theatre association with venues on the Place du Châtelet (Sarah Bernhardt) and Les Abbesses, and it works with partner theatres including Chaillot and the Théâtre de la Cité internationale (theatre website; 2026-27 brochure).

What is there: Italian Renaissance, Flemish and eighteenth-century French works, goldsmiths' work, ceramics, tapestries, Delacroix, Orientalist and Barbizon paintings, portraits by Winterhalter, a Tiepolo ceiling in the dining room and Paolo Uccello's Saint George (museum website;
The Musée Unterlinden is in a former Dominican convent dated to the thirteenth century, listed as a historic monument, in Colmar (Ministry written answer; museum website).

What is there: holdings of modern and contemporary art, fine arts (drawing, print and poster, painting, sculpture) and photography, with Italian painting from the thirteenth to eighteenth centuries, nineteenth-century French and Flemish painting and international contemporary art;
The MAMAC is the Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art of Nice, at Place Yves Klein, and is one of 11 museums run by the City of Nice (museum website).
A house museum at Paseo del General Martínez Campos 37, Madrid, in the house the Sorolla family lived in, with an extension building at Calle Zurbano 68 (Ministry of Culture museum page).

What is there: more than 12,600 pieces in total, of which nearly 5,000 are on show, in painting, sculpture, jewellery, textiles, silverware, archaeology, furniture, numismatics and ivories, drawn from three collections formed in Madrid, Paris and New York over more than sixty years (museum website, history of the collection).
A concert hall at Carrer del Palau de la Música, Barcelona, home of the choirs Orfeó Català, Escola Coral, Cor de Cambra and Palau Vincles (Palau website).
The contemporary art centre of the city of Málaga, now named MUCAC Mayoristas after its merger with the MUPAM into MUCAC (Agencia memorandum 2026).

What is there: the permanent collection is made up entirely of works from the Colección Carmen Thyssen, lent free of charge, with more than 180 works of Spanish and especially Andalusian painting of the 19th and early 20th century and a small selection of older masters from the 13th to 18th centuries (Plan de Actuación 2026).

An arts centre in Santa Cruz de Tenerife in a building designed by Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron with Virgilio Gutiérrez, using diagonal elements and sloping floors so that public space flows into the building and its courtyard (TEA website).
A national archaeological museum at Piazza Museo 18/19, Naples (museum website).
A royal palace complex at Piazza Carlo di Borbone, Caserta, with the Palazzo Reale, Parco Reale, Giardino Inglese, Bosco di San Silvestro and Acquedotto Carolino (museum website).

The Gallerie Nazionali di Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini and Galleria Corsini, a Ministry of Culture institute with sites at Via delle Quattro Fontane 13 and Via della Lungara 10, Rome (programme report 2023).

An opera and ballet house run by the Fondazione Teatro dell'Opera di Roma Capitale, a private-law foundation; venues are the Teatro Costanzi, the Teatro Nazionale, the Teatro Caracalla in summer and the Teatro Valle Franca Valeri (opera website).
An opera and ballet house run by the Fondazione Teatro di San Carlo in Napoli, a private-law foundation with statutes approved by D.M. of 29 December 2014 (Ministry of Culture sheet).
A theatre of Milan with four venues: Teatro Strehler at Largo Greppi 1, Teatro Grassi at Via Rovello 2, Teatro Studio Melato at Via Rivoli 6 and the Chiostro Nina Vinchi (theatre website).
A lyric foundation in Florence; the theatre was built between 2008 and 2014 and has a main hall of 1,890 seats (Il Fatto Quotidiano, 1 March 2023).
A centre for contemporary art at Via Limone 24, Turin, in a 1930s industrial building in Borgo San Paolo, the former Officine Lancia power station (foundation website).
A museum on the roof of the Lingotto in Turin, in the five-storey Scrigno designed by Renzo Piano and built in 2002 (Artribune, 12 March 2022).
The city's old fortress, later renovated into a palace and institutional residence, in Piazza Castello, Turin, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site (museum website).
Teatro Colón is an opera house at Cerrito 628 in Buenos Aires (theatre website).
Teatro Amazonas is an opera house in central Manaus, listed as a historic monument by Iphan since 1966 (Portal Amazônia, 31 July 2024).
Sala São Paulo is the concert hall at Praça Júlio Prestes 16 used by the Orquestra Sinfônica do Estado de São Paulo (Osesp website).
Theatro Municipal is the opera house of Rio de Janeiro, run by the Fundação Theatro Municipal (theatre website).
Museu do Ipiranga is the Museu Paulista of the University of São Paulo, in the Independence monument building at Rua dos Patriotas 100 (museum website).
Museu Oscar Niemeyer is a museum at Rua Marechal Hermes 999, Centro Cívico, Curitiba, in a building by Oscar Niemeyer with an eye-shaped exhibition area (Paraná state tourism page).
What is there: more than 140 works by Diego Rivera and 25 by Frida Kahlo, acquired directly from Rivera, plus archaeological artefacts and crafts.
Museo Franz Mayer occupies a 16th-century building in the historic centre of Mexico City that belonged to the Order of San Juan de Dios and was a hospital until 1966 (museum website).
Museo Nacional de Historia is in the Castillo de Chapultepec in Chapultepec Forest, Mexico City (INAH).
Centro Cultural La Moneda is at Plaza de la Ciudadanía 26, Santiago, run by the Fundación Centro Cultural Palacio de La Moneda (museum website; financial statements).
Museo Nacional de Arqueología, Antropología e Historia del Perú, also called the Museo de Pueblo Libre, is in Pueblo Libre, Lima (Congress of Peru, 10 November 2015).
The Australian War Memorial is at Fairbairn Avenue, Campbell, Canberra (Memorial website).
Arts Centre Melbourne is the Victorian Arts Centre Trust's performing arts complex on St Kilda Road, Melbourne; the annual report calls the building ageing (Annual Report 2023 to 2024).
Opera Australia is a national opera company that performs in the Joan Sutherland Theatre at the Sydney Opera House and in Melbourne (annual report 2024).
Sydney Symphony Orchestra, run by Sydney Symphony Limited, plays in the Concert Hall and Utzon Room at the Sydney Opera House; its office is at Level 17, 56 Pitt Street (orchestra website).
Moderna Museet Malmö is a modern art museum at Ola Billgrens plats 2–4 in Malmö; the page shows the orange facade of the building (museum website).
Artipelag is an exhibition venue at Hålludden on Värmdö, about 30 minutes from Stockholm, with a 9,000 sq. m exhibition hall (museum website;
The Architecture & Design Museum is at Korkeavuorenkatu 23, Helsinki; the old designmuseum.fi address redirects to admuseo.fi (museum website).
The Museum of Applied Arts is at Üllői út 33-37, Budapest, in what its site calls the principal masterpiece of Ödön Lechner; it was modelled on the South Kensington Museum (museum website).
Műcsarnok is at Dózsa György út 37, Budapest, described on its site as home of Hungarian visual art since 1896; it marks its 130th anniversary (museum website).
MMSU, Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Rijeka
The National Museum of Serbia stands on Trg Republike in Belgrade; its new permanent exhibition spans 5,000 m² over three levels from the Palaeolithic to the 20th century (museum website).

The National Museum in Warsaw has a main building and four branches: the Museum of Sculpture in Królikarnia, the Museum of Poster in Wilanów, the Museum of Interiors in Otwock Wielki and the Museum in Nieborów and Arkadia (NIK, Kontrola Państwowa 4/2024).
Wrocław Contemporary Museum

What is there: a National Gallery of Romanian medieval and modern art, a European Art Gallery, an Oriental Art Gallery of nearly 600 objects, a European Decorative Arts Gallery and over 30 collections in the Art Collections Museum (museum website).

The Mariinsky Theatre is in Saint Petersburg; the site's menu lists Mariinsky I, Mariinsky II and the Concert Hall, opera, ballet and orchestra companies, repertoire, and an archive and museum section (theatre website).

The Lviv National Art Gallery is at Stefanyka St. 3 and runs 18 museums and sites, including the Potocki Palace, the Museum of Modernism, Olesko, Zolochiv, Zhovkva and Pidhirtsi castles and the Museum of Old Ukrainian Books (museum website).

A performing arts centre at 1 Esplanade Drive, Singapore, with a Theatre, a Concert Hall, studios, the Singtel Waterfront Theatre (550 seats), an Annexe Studio, an Outdoor Theatre and a Forecourt Garden (Esplanade website).

Dewan Filharmonik PETRONAS (DFP) is a concert hall in the Petronas Twin Towers, Kuala Lumpur, seating 920, designed by Cesar Pelli, with a Klais pipe organ and a recording studio modelled on Abbey Road Studios (annual report 2024).
A museum in Kolkata that, per Live History India (30 Sep 2022), has the highest footfall of any museum in India, often over 2,000 visitors a day on weekdays, and the biggest ticket revenue.

What is there: about 1,500 archaeological objects, some from digs in the UAE and some on loan, including an 18 m reconstruction of a Bronze Age Magan trading ship and a cuneiform tablet that describes it (The Art Newspaper, 2 Dec 2025).
A natural history museum of 35,000 sq m in the Saadiyat Cultural District, designed by the Dutch firm Mecanoo (The Art Newspaper, 2 Dec 2025).
A multi-format venue of over 35,500 sq m built-up area in the Opera District, Downtown Dubai, near the Burj Khalifa (Gulf News).
The official museum of Saudi Arabia, on the east side of the main square of the King Abdulaziz Historical Center, Al Murabba district, Riyadh (Saudipedia).
The opera house in Cairo, home to the Egyptian ballet and opera company (Al Jazeera, 3 Jun 2013).
A museum on Robben Island, Cape Town, which the museum's site describes as a World Heritage Site (museum website).

A theatre in Newtown, Johannesburg, one of the main artistic hubs of the Market Theatre Foundation, which comprises the Market Theatre, Market Laboratory and Market Photo Workshop (Mail & Guardian, 22 Apr 2023); the council also oversees the Windybrow Arts Centre (The Citizen, 23 Oct 2025).
Shakespeare's Globe is a reconstructed Elizabethan open-air playhouse with an indoor Sam Wanamaker Playhouse, at 21 New Globe Walk on Bankside, London (museum website).

The Royal Court Theatre is a new-writing theatre at Sloane Square, London, with the Jerwood Theatre Downstairs and the Jerwood Theatre Upstairs, run by the charity The English Stage Company Limited (accounts 2025).
The Young Vic is a theatre at 66 The Cut, London, run by the charity The Young Vic Company (accounts 2025).
Sadler's Wells runs four London venues: Sadler's Wells Theatre and the Lilian Baylis Studio at Angel, the Peacock Theatre in the West End and Sadler's Wells East in Stratford (museum website).

The Royal Shakespeare Company is a theatre company based at Stratford-upon-Avon, with the Royal Shakespeare Theatre, the Swan Theatre and The Other Place (a new-writing hub with a Studio Theatre of up to 250 seats), and productions in London such as Matilda the Musical at the Cambridge Theatre (annual report 2025).

The Royal Albert Hall is a Grade I listed concert hall in Kensington, London, run by the Corporation of the Hall of Arts and Sciences, a Royal Charter body and registered charity (annual report 2024).

The Edinburgh International Festival is an annual three-week August festival of music, theatre, opera and dance in Edinburgh, run by the Edinburgh International Festival Society, a charity based at The Hub, Castlehill (annual report 2025).
The Abbey Theatre (Amharclann na Mainistreach) is the National Theatre of Ireland, at 26 Lower Abbey Street, Dublin 1, with the Abbey and Peacock stages (financial statements 2024).
